reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports Al-Ni driven clustering and the temperature dependence of SRO in the Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni system, but it does not address nanoalloys, the effect of quenching vs. annealing on SRO, or the causal link between pre-existing SRO and subsequent high-temperature stability. E3 discusses B2 phase formation linked to Al-Ni SRO in bulk HEAs, not nanoalloys. Thus, key premises about processing control of SRO and its mediating role in nanoalloy stability are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous single-phase solid solution in high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperatures.
Local chemical short-range order (SRO), driven by favorable pair correlations (e.g., Al-Ni), promotes clustering or phase separation.
Rapid quenching minimizes SRO, while slower annealing enhances it.
The pre-existing level of SRO mediates the nanoalloy's structural stability under subsequent high-temperature exposure.
In the Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni system, Al-Ni correlations specifically drive clustering behavior.
